render.always: THE PROPHET: an older silver-haired man with a short white beard, in a long pale cream traveling coat over simple linen clothes, carrying a tall dark-wood staff with a small brass bell at its head, and a polished brass speaking-trumpet slung on a leather strap across his chest. Warm, theatrical, entirely confident; a famous guide people follow in crowds. He is NEVER sinister and never a villain; his failure is timing, not malice. NO religious iconography of any tradition: no cross, no robes of any faith, no halo. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal.

master.bake: Standing full-body, front three-quarter, one hand on the staff, the brass trumpet on its strap, mid-proclamation warmth on his face.

prose.voice: Ringing, certain, generous in the way a stage is generous. He is not lying; he is late by construction, because a channel a million people can hear is a channel whose news is already old.
prose.lore: An ARCHETYPE, never a named real person: the famous herald with a million followers who announces an elevator's location to everyone at once, after the seats are already full. He exists so the book can dismiss broadcast as a channel without dismissing the man.
prose.rules: Depict with warmth and scale (crowds, banners without lettering, a high rock to speak from), never with menace. He must not resemble any specific living person. No religious iconography of any tradition; he is a startup-world archetype in fable dress.
